concepts.title: Rotation of the Earth: Day and Night

questions.a: The earth's rotation on its axis once every 24 hours turns each side toward and away from the sun.

questions.q: How long does one rotation of the earth take?
Why does the sun appear to rise in the east?
questions.a: The earth spins from west to east, so the sun seems to move across the sky from east to west.

concepts.title: Revolution of the Earth and the Seasons

questions.a: The earth's tilted axis as it revolves around the sun - each hemisphere gets more or less direct sunlight through the year.

questions.q: How long does one revolution of the earth take?
questions.a: About 365 and a quarter days - one year.

questions.q: Why is it summer in India when it is winter in Australia?
questions.a: Earth's tilt aims the sun's rays more directly at one hemisphere, then the other.
The moon coming between the sun and earth so its shadow hides the sun for some places.
The earth coming between the sun and moon so earth's shadow darkens the full moon.
The sun, earth and moon must line up exactly, which happens only a few times a year.

concepts.title: Modelling the Sky with Globe and Shadows

questions.q: How can a globe model day and night?
questions.a: Spinning a globe before a lamp shows half the earth lit (day) and half dark (night).

questions.q: What does the shadow of a stick at noon tell us?
questions.a: Its shortest shadow points north-south and shows the sun is highest (and which way is south).

questions.q: How did sailors use shadows and stars to find directions?
questions.a: The noon shadow gave north-south; the Pole Star at night points to the north.
